verdict: Rippling: Choose Rippling when you want HR, payroll, and IT on one employee record and will model stacked PEPM — not when you only need simple US payroll or a dedicated ATS. Scores use the HR editorial methodology from first-party research as of 2026-08-17 — not hands-on product testing.
strengths: Unifies HR, payroll, and IT on one employee system of record
Published SMB PEPM floor (with clear module-stacking caveat)
Time, recruiting, spend, and EOR available as modules
Ask Rippling AI across workforce data
weaknesses: All-in TCO is quote-stacked far above $8 PEPM
Implementation heavier than payroll-first SMB tools
Not a specialist ATS or hospitality WFM
bestFor: Companies that want HR, payroll, and IT provisioning on one employee record
Fast-growing teams willing to model modular PEPM TCO
Orgs that currently stitch HRIS + Okta/MDM + payroll and want one hire event
notIdealFor: Teams that only need simple US payroll (Gusto is the lighter start)
Buyers who want a dedicated ATS as the primary purchase (Greenhouse)
Frontline-only operators shopping for shift scheduling apps
tradeoffs: Published free tiers vs paid depth for ATS, WFM, time, or training jobs
Hub / multi-module pricing complexity vs single-product floors
Mobile/frontline readiness vs desk-bound admin depth
Opaque contact-sales pricing vs transparent published seats
recommendation: Choose Rippling when you want HR, payroll, and IT on one employee record and will model stacked PEPM — not when you only need simple US payroll or a dedicated ATS. Compare BambooHR for a simpler core HRIS, Gusto for payroll-first SMB buying, Greenhouse for structured hiring, and Workday for enterprise HCM.
editorialNotes: HR Priority-1 batch. Approved on hr-editorial v1.0.0. membershipRole=primary. jobCluster=people-platform. handsOnTesting=false. Affiliate economics excluded.

criterionAssessments.rationale: Powerful modular platform with more setup than BambooHR or Gusto. Score reflects breadth versus a simple payroll-first UI — not hands-on lab testing.
Primary job is people-platform: HR + payroll + IT on one employee record. Scored inside that cluster, not as a dedicated ATS or frontline WFM.
Hire-to-device-to-pay workflows are the product thesis. Recruiting and time exist as modules; depth is strongest as a unified employee graph.
650+ apps plus native device/app provisioning is category-leading ecosystem depth for a people platform.
Employee/manager mobile and time exist; not a deskless scheduling specialist. Scored for people-platform mobility.
Workforce reporting across HR/IT/spend is a published strength versus single-module HRIS tools.
Modular PEPM and global/EOR paths support growth from SMB into mid-market; enterprise HCM is still a different shortlist.
Published $8 floor is misleading versus stacked TCO. Held at 6 for packaging opacity. Affiliate economics excluded.
Ask Rippling AI is marketed across workforce data — useful assistant story with quote-gated packaging.

overallScoreRationale: Weighted average of the nine HR editorial criteria using the category weights (hiring/workforce fit 15, workflow depth 14, ease of use 12, integrations 12, value 12, mobile/frontline 10, scalability 9, analytics 8, AI 8), rounded to 1 decimal. Products are scored inside their job cluster — ATS, core HRIS, payroll/benefits, people-platform, frontline WFM, time & attendance, SOP training, and LMS peers are not forced into one undifferentiated ranking. Not a hands-on lab score, and affiliate economics are excluded.
